excerpt: Weapons law governs the tools, methods, and technologies used in armed conflict, limiting weapons that cause superfluous injury, unnecessary suffering, indiscriminate effects, or uncontrollable civilian harm. This article explains prohibited means of warfare, restricted weapons, weapons reviews, chemical and biological weapons, mines, cluster munitions, blinding lasers, incendiary weapons, explosive remnants of war, nuclear weapons, explosive weapons in populated areas, drones, cyber operations, autonomous weapons systems, AI-enabled targeting, space-enabled warfare, environmental harm, and weapons transfers. It examines how treaty law, customary international humanitarian law, Article 36 reviews, command responsibility, proportionality, distinction, humanity, and precautions shape legal analysis before, during, and after deployment. By connecting doctrine, technology, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how international law evaluates not only what weapons are, but how they are designed, reviewed, transferred, used, and investigated.
